code.originalText: Review four weeks after stone removal and prostate resection, with urate titration and stone metabolic evaluation

text.paragraph: Review four weeks after stone removal and prostate resection. [S]

Mr. Franklin returns four weeks after transurethral laser cystolitholapaxy and resection of the prostate. The catheter came out on the second day after surgery. His stream is strong, he gets up once at night, and he has had no pain or blood in the urine for two weeks. Stone analysis showed pure uric acid. He has had no gout flare on allopurinol 200 mg and colchicine. The planned urate check two to five weeks after the dose increase was not done, because his surgery fell in that window. He completed a 24-hour urine collection yesterday. He drinks about 1.5 L a day and finds it hard to drink more. Tamsulosin was stopped at surgery. [S]

list.item:
Uric acid bladder stone, removed (N21.0). Stone-free, with the obstruction relieved. The 24-hour urine shows the main risks for another uric acid stone: low urine volume (1.45 L), high uric acid excretion (840 mg a day), and acidic urine (pH 5.3). Citrate (410 mg a day) and calcium (180 mg a day) are normal. Red cells in the urine have cleared (1 per high-power field), so no further hematuria imaging is needed. [S]
Start potassium citrate 10 mEq twice daily with meals, aiming for a urine pH of 6.0 to 6.5.
Raise fluids to make at least 2.5 L of urine a day; a measuring jug at home.
Potassium check in 2 to 4 weeks, because he also takes losartan and has chronic kidney disease.

Gout, titrating (M1A.0710). Serum urate 6.4 mg/dL on allopurinol 200 mg, still above the target of below 6. [S]
Increase allopurinol to 300 mg daily.
Continue colchicine prophylaxis.
Serum urate in 2 to 5 weeks.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia after resection (N40.1). IPSS 6 and residual 35 mL, down from 16 and 160 mL; pathology benign. [S]
Reassess IPSS and residual at three and six months after surgery.

Chronic kidney disease G3a A1 (N18.31). Creatinine 1.31 mg/dL, eGFR 56, potassium 4.5 mmol/L; stable after surgery. [S]
Continue losartan and atorvastatin.

Hypertension (I10). 132/78 mmHg; home average 132/78. [S]
Continue losartan; recheck at the next review.
